schema_note: Machine-readable facts for the EX280V422 exam, OCP 4.22 product docs, and the game's EX280 Prep mode (docs/CONVERSION-SPEC.md section 11). All externally sourced claims are cited in sources[]; internal game-plan references are clearly marked.
exam_name: Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration
exam_name_on_redhat_com_page: Red Hat Certified System Administrator in OpenShift exam (EX280)
naming_note: Naming is inconsistent between Red Hat sources as of 2026-11-03: redhat.com/en/services/training/red-hat-certified-openshift-administrator-exam is titled 'Red Hat Certified System Administrator in OpenShift exam' and says passing makes you a 'Red Hat Certified System Administrator in OpenShift', while the LMS 'Exam Objectives by Version' PDF lists 'EX280K - Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration'. The objectives list for EX280V422 is identical in both sources. Ask the Lead which display name the game should use; CONVERSION-SPEC.md currently uses 'Red Hat Certified Specialist in OpenShift Administration (EX280V422)'.
exam_delivery: Hands-on, performance-based practical exam; candidates perform routine system tasks on a live OpenShift Container Platform 4.22 system to meet specific objective criteria. Relevant product documentation is available during the exam, but no outside assistance is allowed.
performance_rule: Configurations and services must persist and remain functional across the normal lifecycle of the platform without requiring manual intervention to restore or start them (LMS PDF: 'configurations must persist after reboot without intervention').
results: Scores are reported by Red Hat Certification Central via email, usually within 3 U.S. business days. Results are reported as total scores only; Red Hat does not report performance on individual items or provide extra detail on request.

scoring_and_validity.note: The exam page specifies that results are total scores but does not state a passing score, score scale, or certification validity period. The Red Hat Certification Program Guide is linked from the exam page and covers official policy, but its content could not be extracted (docs.redhat.com page is JS-rendered; PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 to this agent, and no Wayback snapshot was available). Do not state a passing score or validity period in game copy without re-verifying via https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_learning_subscription/1-latest/html/red_hat_certification_program_guide/index .

prerequisites.stated: No formal prerequisite. Recommended preparation listed on the exam page:
recommended: Red Hat System Administration I (RH124) or comparable experience; Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA) strongly recommended but not required
Red Hat OpenShift Administration I: Containers & Kubernetes (DO180) or comparable work experience using OpenShift Container Platform
Red Hat OpenShift Administration II: Operating a Production Kubernetes Cluster (DO280) or comparable work experience using OpenShift Container Platform
Experience with container technology is recommended
prerequisites.do280_note: The DO280 course name printed on the exam page is 'Red Hat OpenShift Administration II: Operating a Production Kubernetes Cluster'. The redhat.com DO280 course page returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-11-03, so the current official course outline could not be fetched. A partner-hosted outline (New Horizons / DO280LS, based on OCP 4.14) was used only as a secondary, possibly stale cross-check; it still lists an 'OpenShift Updates' chapter that is no longer in the V422 objective list.

version_sensitive_flags.detail: DeploymentConfig (apps.openshift.io/v1) is deprecated as of OCP 4.14; still supported in 4.22 but not recommended, only security/critical fixes. New work (and the exam's declarative-manifest tasks) should use apps/v1 Deployment / ReplicaSet. DeploymentConfig-only features still exist (native triggers, deployer pod, custom strategies) and the deployer service account may not exist if the DeploymentConfig capability is disabled.

Since OCP 4.16 a long-lived service account API token Secret is no longer auto-generated for each service account. Use `oc create token <sa>` (bound/temporary token) or project a serviceAccountToken volume; existing long-lived tokens continue to work after upgrade.
`oc export` is a removed 3.x command and does not appear in the OCP 4.22 CLI reference; use `oc get <resource> -o yaml > file.yaml` (plus oc create/apply/replace) to export/import resources.

version_sensitive_flags.topic: Default SCC for authenticated users is restricted-v2 (restricted-v3 also documented for new 4.22 installs)
version_sensitive_flags.detail: All authenticated users are granted restricted-v2 by default; privileged is NOT granted by default. The 4.22 SCC docs table also says restricted-v3 'is the most restrictive SCC provided by a new installation and will be used by default for authenticated users', so verify on the target cluster (`oc get scc`, `oc adm policy who-can use scc restricted-v3`). `oc adm policy add-scc-to-user privileged -z <sa>` is the documented way to allow a privileged workload. Setting privileged: true in a Pod spec does not by itself select the privileged SCC. SCCs still govern admission in 4.22 and are synchronized with Pod Security Admission labels.

version_sensitive_flags.topic: Kustomize and Helm are explicit V422 bullets (already named in V412K/V414K)
version_sensitive_flags.detail: The LMS PDF's V412K/V414K section already lists 'Use Kustomize overlays to modify application configurations' and 'Deploy applications from images, OpenShift templates, and Helm charts'. V422 splits these into the explicit bullets 'Deploy applications using Kustomize', 'Work with Kustomize overlays' and 'Deploy applications from templates and Helm charts' (plus the standalone 'Work with resource manifests' bullet). OCP 4.22 product docs contain only limited Kustomize coverage (CLI reference for `oc apply -k`/`oc kustomize` plus a MicroShift job page); Helm is documented through the Helm CLI install page, HelmChartRepository CR and web-console Helm releases.

version_sensitive_flags.topic: Old objective sections removed in V422
version_sensitive_flags.detail: V412K had a 'Manage storage for application configuration and data' section (PVs, storage classes, StatefulSets) and a 'Configure applications for reliability' section (probes, resource limits, scaling). V414K had an 'Update OpenShift' section (cluster updates, deprecated API usage, operator updates). None of these are separate sections in EX280V422. Storage still appears only implicitly (secrets/configmaps, PVCs used by templates or stateful workloads), and updates are not an objective. Do not make them primary game content.

version_sensitive_flags.topic: OLM v0 vs OLM v1 (Operator Framework)
version_sensitive_flags.detail: OCP 4.22 docs contain both classic Operator Lifecycle Manager content (Subscription/OperatorGroup/CSV/InstallPlan, operators guide) and newer 'Extensions' OLM v1 content (catalogd/operator-controller). EX280 operator tasks are most consistent with classic OLM v0 (OperatorHub, Subscription, CSV) and the game's planned Subscription model; flag OLM v1 as out of scope unless Red Hat says otherwise.

The default project template used for self-service project creation is `project-request` in the `openshift-config` project (older OCP docs referenced other namespaces). Customize it with `oc edit template project-request -n openshift-config`; NetworkPolicies can be added to its objects list.

Routes are route.openshift.io/v1. TLS termination types: edge (router terminates, cert/key on route), passthrough (router does not terminate; no cert/key on route; path-based routing unavailable), reencrypt (terminate then re-encrypt; needs destinationCACertificate). Cross-namespace hostname claims are controlled by IngressController .spec.routeAdmission.namespaceOwnership (default Strict).

game_plan_reference.note: Internal, not an external citation: game curriculum/challenge/EX280 Prep design lives in docs/CONVERSION-SPEC.md sections 9-11. Current shipped content: 20 OpenShift campaign levels in 5 chapters, 12 timed challenge labs, and 36 incident definitions (see js/data/CampaignLevels.js, js/modes/ChallengeMode.js, js/data/IncidentDefs.js).
